To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the current‐noise power spectra of hydrogenated amorphouseilicon thin‐film transisitors (TFTs), fabricated from a‐Si:H, can be predicted to within a factor of about 10 by theories developed for metal–oxide–semiconductor field‐effect transisitors.

the current noise power spectra of hydrogenated amorphouseilicon thin‐film transis tors are in agreement with theories developed for crystallinesilicon field effect transistors, and that the noise in the nonconducting regime is proportional to the square of the current.
TFTs fabricated from hydrogenated a‐Si:H are noisier than their crystalline counterparts.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a high‐performance thin‐film transistor technology for use in active‐matrix liquid‐crystal‐display (AM LCD) panels.
the fabrication, characterization, and applications of hydrogenated amorphousand microcrystalline silicon thin film transistors.
the development of a high‐speed, low‐power, and low‐cost technology for the production of large‐scale integrated circuits.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the noise in TFTs can be predicted by the theories developed for MOSFETs.
the current noise in the TFTs is a function of the leakage current, and is not related to any of the physical parameters that have been proposed.
current fluctuations in amorphous silicon TFTs can be predicted from the noise behavior of metal‐oxide field effect transistors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the TFT current noise is a function of the TFT leakage current and is not dependent on the TFT channel length.
the noise in the conducting mode can be predicted by existing theories, while the noise in the nonconducting state is a new phenomenon which has not been previously observed in crystalline TFTs.
TFTs are good devices for low‐frequency noise measurements.
The main takeaway from our work is that
TFTs fabricated from amorphous silicon are not fundamentally different from their crystalline counterparts.
the current noise in amorphous silicon TFTs can be predicted by the existing models for crystalline TFTs.
amorphous silicon TFTs are a viable option for applications that do not require low noise performance.
